correctness.rationale: With uniform vertex masses, unit edges and real potentials, anchoring one vertex turns the bounded Lipschitz polytope into a totally-unimodular directed-incidence system; all its vertices are integral. Strict convexity of centered L4^4 means every maximizer is a vertex. Diameter<=2 and tight-edge constraints reduce integer extremizers to binary indicators or plus/minus signs confined to one part, zero off that part. Exact moment expansions give B_N(k) and T_{N,m}(t); strict one-coordinate convexity shows only the largest part matters. Comparing adjacent parity-lattice t values establishes the finite threshold and the limiting optimization has switches m/N=1/12 and 2/3. Independent exact enumeration over 37 multipartite part-size types with N<=7 verified all maximum numerators; universal result follows from analytical reduction.

value.rationale: The centered Lipschitz-to-L4 norm is a natural higher-moment graph spread invariant. An exact all-parameters functional and complete optimizer family, with a binary-to-polarized transition at 1/12 and a distinct macroscopic imbalance threshold at 2/3, provide a quantitatively meaningful new phase diagram beyond the known L2 spread; parity effects are mathematically substantive. Not a claim to have discovered the already classified polytope facets.

limitations: 37 graph configurations with <=7 vertices were exhaustively checked only over integral feasible labels; real-parameter result rests on the strict convex integral-vertex proof.
Uniform masses and fourth unstandardized centered moment only.
